newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha weaker, seen in correctionary phase.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha weaker, seen in correctionary phase.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices were lower on Monday, with sellers outnumbering buyers as weak sentiment from Friday continued to permeate the market, traders said.
"Naphtha is failing to keep up with crude's gains today on the ACCESS system," a trader said. "The underlying tone is still firm, but the market needed a correction," he said.
Open-spec naphtha first-half March was at $247.50/249.00, and second-half March at $245.00/246.50, down compared to $250.00/251.50 and $247.00/248.50, respectively, on Friday.
Some traders said a poor supply/demand situation was pressuring the market.
Japanese and South Korean end-users have mostly covered needs for first-half February, but are expected to buy more cargoes for the second-half of the month, traders said.

Nationwide strikes in South Korea are not effecting the market, traders said. On Friday, unionised workers at three South Korean petrochemical firms said they would go on a two-day partial strike from Tuesday. Union representatives said the strike was not expected to cause production losses. Traders said the oil spill from a Russian tanker on Monday was not effecting LSWR. Authorities are placing priority on keeping oil away from nuclear plants, which use sea water as a coolant.
